label: <DEL> step (and first copy step) in long sequences rich in d/h/i/x/y/v or starting with c/f/0/z
explanation: Never fires in the original phase. 80% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (recall_idx 0) and about 20% at the first copy step (recall_idx 1); almost nothing later. Only about 10% of <DEL> steps fire, and rate rises steeply with L (L=9 has 52% of mass, L<=5 almost none). Which <DEL> steps fire depends on sequence content in a graded way: firing is more likely when the original tokens include several of d/h/i/x/y/v, and when the first token (the one about to be output) is c/f/0/z (rate about 6-7x). The top examples, e.g. c d h x h d h j t, combine both. When the first token is p, activation can move to the first copy step. This reads like a distributed content code at the start of recall, not a crisp condition; the predicate reaches dev F1 0.41 and mass recall 0.65.
